set.approach: Park at the Bow Lake lot and walk along the shore to the gully, or head straight across the lake when it is frozen solid. The gully stays hidden until you are close, although the top of the last pitch can be seen from lake level. Allow an hour or two for the walk.
set.descent_text: Rappel the line of ascent from the bolted anchors. The belay in the middle of the route can be skipped, so a long single rope or a pair of ropes both work.

review.notes: Approach and the rappel-the-route descent from the route page and area page; counts left out.

set.approach: From the Bow Glacier lot the falls are in view to the southwest. Follow the signed trail along the lake edge, or cross the ice directly if the lake is frozen solid, to the moraine below the cirque that holds the flow. The walk takes an hour or two.
set.descent_text: Parties get down by rappelling the route.

review.notes: Approach from area and route pages; descent is the single line the route page gives.

set.approach: These flows hang a short way to the right of Bow Falls, so walk the Bow Falls approach from the Bow Glacier lot (lake edge, or across the frozen lake, to the moraine) and continue to the right. They do not form every season.
set.descent_text: Rappel from ice-screw anchors and v-threads.

review.notes: Location and rappel anchors from the route page; approach shared with Bow Falls.

set.approach: Park at the Rockbound Lake trailhead and follow the signs for Silverton Falls, a short walk. To climb from the bottom, step over the wooden barricade just before the switchbacks and follow the creek into the canyon. If the lower pools are open and cannot be crossed, take the switchbacks to the viewpoint and scramble down to the foot of the last two tiers.
set.descent_text: From the tree belay at the top, walk up and to the left on a steep walk-off that rejoins the tourist trail.

review.notes: Single page: parking, signed path, canyon entry, bypass viewpoint and walk-off.

set.approach: Park in the lot at the wardens complex on Mount Crandell, below the gullies that show from the road into the townsite, and hike up to the leftmost obvious gully. The walk is short but steep, and takes longer in deep snow. These slopes carry avalanche hazard, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from v-threads. Hiking off to climber's left is possible but unpleasant.

review.notes: Parking, gully choice, descent options from the route page; area page agrees on the lot and a short approach.

set.approach: Park at the wardens complex lot and hike nearly straight up to the right-most of the three gullies visible from the road, ending at the foot of the first ice pitch. The walk is short but takes longer in deep snow. Avalanche hazard is present, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach only; the route page gives no descent.

ab_devils_thumb_no_nuts_no_glory.skip_reason: no page for this route found in any source; nothing to base an approach or descent on

set.approach: Follow the Marmot Basin ski road to the second-to-last switchback below the ski area lot. Park higher up where there is space, walk back down to the switchback and step over the railing. The trail through the woods is usually obvious and reaches the gully in a few minutes; the flows are up that gully.
set.descent_text: Rappel from trees or a bolted ring at the top to a large snow ledge, then cross the ledge to a bolted boulder and rappel the lower flow.

review.notes: Access from the area page, anchors and rappel route from the route page.

set.approach: Park east of Stony Creek at the ranger station driveway off Highway 541 and walk east a couple of hundred metres to an obvious creek on the left. Follow the creek bed north; when it becomes too hard, sidehill on the slope above and drop back in where it makes sense. It is a long approach of several hours, with short steps of approach ice, to a split in the drainage with rolling ice on the left. Past a prominent hanging tower, turn left through the trees into a side gully, which holds the climb.
set.descent_text: Come down the way you came, rappelling from v-threads and trees and reversing the approach drainage.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; trailhead from the area page.

ab_holy_cross_mountain_holy_cross_east.skip_reason: its only page places the approach at a different trailhead from the rest of Holy Cross Mountain and gives no descent; not verifiable

set.approach: Park east of Stony Creek at the ranger station driveway off Highway 541 and walk east a couple of hundred metres to a creek on the left. Follow the creek bed north, then sidehill above it where it gets hard, returning to the drainage later. After a long approach of several hours reach a split with rolling ice on the left, then climb a series of short ice steps; the pillar shows up above and to the left.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the two small trees at the belay on the left and reverse the approach.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; trailhead from the area page.

set.approach: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Waterfowl Lake, hike around the lake, then climb through forest and a moraine to reach the base of the face.

review.notes: Approach only; the sources do not say where the route ends or how parties come down.

set.approach: Park at the Maligne Canyon lot off Maligne Lake Road, follow the tourist path down to the canyon floor, and walk up the canyon past the ice-walk traffic to the flow. Anchors are off trees.

review.notes: Approach only; no descent given.

set.approach: Park at the Maligne Canyon lot and follow the tourist path to the canyon bottom. Pass through the gate, put on crampons, and walk up the canyon floor; the short steps can be soloed or belayed from ice on the floor. The floor can be covered by thin ice over running water, so test your footing.
set.descent_text: The canyon route ends with a walk out from the top back to the parking area.

review.notes: Approach and walk-out from the route page.

set.approach: Park at the Maligne Canyon lot off Maligne Lake Road, follow the tourist path down to the canyon, and walk up the canyon floor to the wall. The anchor is an obvious tree.

review.notes: Approach only; no descent given.

set.approach: Park at the Maligne Canyon lot off Maligne Lake Road, follow the tourist path down to the canyon, and walk up the canyon floor to the free-standing column. Anchors are off trees.

review.notes: Approach only; no descent given.

set.approach: The walk from the road is short and easy. Walk up the snowcoach road toward the coach lot and pick up the climbers' trail into the moraines just before it. For the northeast face, bear left when below the shared Athabasca and Andromeda glacier, and keep the rope on while crossing it.
set.descent_text: Walk to the AA col, descend the glacier from there, and return to the road.

review.notes: Approach from area and route pages; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Start from the higher car park on the Andromeda side of the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre. Walk up the glacier-tour road until it drops toward the ice, then follow an occasionally cairned trail up toward the prominent gully you can see from the lot, just below the icefall. Stay low enough to keep off the glacier but high enough to avoid losing elevation. It is a long approach, well over an hour.

review.notes: Approach only; the descent text is the writer's belief, not a stated fact.

set.approach: Follow the Andromeda approach: up the snowcoach road, onto the moraines, then contour along them to the north bowl glacier. Head up that small glacier past the foot of the better-known routes Andromeda Strain and Asteroid Alley, roped on the ice. The line is the right-most of several large ice-filled gullies on the north face.
set.descent_text: Descend the east ridge to the AA col, then go down toward the glacier; v-thread rappels are used on the col side.

review.notes: Approach from area and route pages; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Walk up the snowcoach road to the moraines and contour along them to the north bowl glacier, staying roped. Angle left toward the north bowl, threading crevasses, and cross the bergschrund. The line lies left of the north bowl route, between rock bands on the left and the left edge of a serac on the right.
set.descent_text: Descend by the AA col.

review.notes: Approach from the area page plus the route's own text; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Walk up the snowcoach road, follow the climbers' trail into the moraines, and contour along them to the north bowl glacier, roped on the ice. The route is left of Skyladder, roughly in the middle of the face.
set.descent_text: Walk around to the AA col and descend from there.

review.notes: Approach shared across the north-side routes; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Park at the pullout by the snowcoach gate and walk up the snowcoach road, then take the trail on the left up the moraine to the foot of the glacier. Cross the glacier beneath the Silverhorn and the north face; the line climbs the left-hand side of that face.
set.descent_text: Go down across the false summit called the Silverhorn, then along the shoulder past it.

review.notes: Approach from area and Regular North Face pages; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Follow the Regular North Face approach: up the snowcoach road, the moraine trail to the foot of the glacier, then up the glacier trending left to the col below the Silverhorn. The variation runs a short way left of the usual finish.
set.descent_text: Any of the standard ways down will do, including the AA col or the regular route on the mountain.

review.notes: Approach shared with Regular North Face; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Park at the pullout by the snowcoach gate and walk up the snowcoach road to the staging area. A trail on the left of the road climbs the moraine to a rocky shoulder where the glacier begins; then climb the glacier trending left to the col below the Silverhorn, where the face is obvious. Head up the face toward a large yellow rock and on to a gap in the small rock band.
set.descent_text: From the summit go down to a small col, climb to the top of the Silverhorn, and descend to the AA col, where two options split. The safer one bears left on steep slopes onto the AA glacier; keep right on it until a rock cliff ends the ice, then a trail returns to the snowcoach road. In good conditions the other goes right and down the north glacier, rejoining the approach.

review.notes: Single detailed page.

set.approach: Follow the Regular North Face approach: the snowcoach road, the moraine trail to the glacier, then up the glacier trending left. The route is a narrow ice gully at the right-hand end of the rock bands, just short of the hanging seracs.
set.descent_text: Descend by the north glacier.

review.notes: Approach per the route page; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Begin at the Moraine Lake lot and walk the tourist trail to the far end of the lake. Where the boardwalk ends, cross the creek and follow the climbers' trail through a boulderfield toward a big wall. Cairns lead up ledges to a chimney with a rappel anchor, then a short vertical wall with a chain, and a bolted traverse to another rappel point. A scramble leads to a bench below the glacier, where camping is possible. Then go southwest up the glacier toward the Neil Colgan hut or on to the face, depending on crevasses.
set.descent_text: Descend by the west ridge or the south side. The south side is slow, its gully line is not obvious, rappel stations on the back side may not be found, and it ends with a walk around another peak back to the hut.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; descent options from the route page.

set.approach: Begin at the Moraine Lake lot and walk the tourist trail to the far end of the lake. Where the boardwalk ends, cross the creek and follow the climbers' trail through a boulderfield toward a big wall. Follow cairns up ledges to a chimney with a rappel anchor, then a vertical wall with a chain and a bolted traverse, to a bench below the glacier. Cross the glacier toward the Neil Colgan hut; the route is the last one on the left of the face.
set.descent_text: Descend the west ridge and return to the hut by the Perren route.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Use the roadside pullout a few minutes north of Bow Summit. Descend and cross the river, then ski or hike through trees and up a rib to enter the bowl under the line, serious avalanche terrain; check the avalanche forecast. Several hundred feet of steep snow lead to the base, where you dig out a belay platform.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. A bolted anchor sits at the top, but most parties rappel from v-threads.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; pullout from the area page.

set.approach: Park on the roadside about a kilometre toward Jasper from the Icefield Centre, where the route is visible from the road. Use skis to cross the gravel flats and reach the moraines, pass a small icefall on your right, and climb the snow cone to the base. Camping the night before is common. This is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: On the ice cap stay roped and head left across the glacier, avoiding the corniced left edge, to the saddle between Snowdome and Little Snowdome. Traverse back into the descent gully, farther than you expect. Rappel a mellow rock band, then make several ice rappels until the gully flattens and you can walk back to the base.

review.notes: Single detailed page.

set.approach: Park in the Sunshine Village lot, walk past the gondolas to its far end, and pick up the creekside trail. Higher up, work up and to the right over ice steps in the gully or over rock slabs to the base. The route is well left of Bourgeau Right-Hand and not visible until you are below it. Large avalanche slopes lie above, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route using the fixed stations.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; avalanche terrain from the area page.

set.approach: Park in the Sunshine Village lot; the route can be seen up and to the right. Go through the trees up the right side of the drainage, crossing it once or more, with some rock scrambling. The last stretch is usually best taken up the left side of the bowl and then back right. Large avalanche slopes lie above, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the top to the snow slope and scramble down to the trees. Further rappels down the route reach the base, skipping some of the anchors. All belay and rappel anchors are fixed; bring cord to refresh the slings.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; avalanche terrain from the area page.

ab_mt_deltaform_super_couloir.skip_reason: its only page declines to give route beta; no approach or descent text to draw on

set.approach: Start at the Heart Creek lot and take the link trail heading west toward the Bow Corridor and turn into the first drainage, less than 100 m away. Go up the climber's left side of the drainage, following flagging to a trail through the trees that avoids the cliff bands partway up, then emerge in the amphitheatre under the ice. Considerable avalanche hazard exists above, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the slung small tree at the top to the anchors at the base of the last pitch; if the anchors cannot be found, there is enough ice for a v-thread. Continue anchor to anchor down the line to the snow slope below the second pitch, then walk climber's left to easier ground and down to the start.

review.notes: Single detailed page.

set.approach: The route sits far up Protection Valley, a remote side valley tucked behind Castle Mountain, on its right-hand side; access is easiest when snow is low. Scramble up a steep slope to a comfortable belay station at the base. The slope is avalanche prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach only; the page gives no descent.

set.approach: Drive up the Akamina road toward Cameron Lake to the drainage of the Quick and Dirty amphitheatre, which has room for several cars. French Kiss is the first obvious icefall on the right as you head toward the lake, and the left-most flow in the amphitheatre.

review.notes: Approach from route and area pages; no stated descent.

set.approach: Drive up the Akamina road toward Cameron Lake to the drainage with space for several cars, then walk up into the amphitheatre. The route is the obvious flow on the right side of the amphitheatre, with French Kiss as the left-most flow.

review.notes: Approach from area and French Kiss pages; no stated descent.
